newsitem.title: USA: California's Yosemite Park damage put at $178 mln.
newsitem.headline: California's Yosemite Park damage put at $178 mln.

text.p: The cost of repairing Yosemite National Park in California, which was badly damaged by storms and floods in January, is estimated at $178 million, Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt said.
The estimate is based on a comprehensive assessment of visible flood damage and estimates for moving facilities to more suitable locations, the Interior Department said.
Roads, sewers, buildings and campgrounds in Yosemite National Park, 150 miles southeast of San Francisco, were badly damaged by floods early in January.
Damage estimates are expected to climb once the snow has melted and crews are able to get into areas inaccessible during the winter, the Interior Department said.
Some parts of the huge park have reopened since the flood but Yosemite Valley, which houses park headquarters and much of the lodging, remains closed.
"We are committed to reopening the park as quickly as possible," Babbitt said in a statement. "Emergency repairs are under way to stabilize the infrastructure, but the long-term fix will take time."

He added, "To fully reopen the park and assist the gateway communities' economy will require action by Congress. We ... look forward to working with Congress to gain the funding necessary for full recovery of the park."
Yosemite National Park Superintendent B.J. Griffin said the key to rebuilding intelligently was to learn from the mistakes of the past.
"Buildings and campgrounds constructed in the flood area will be replaced in scale, scope and function, but relocated away from the flood zone," he said.
